key_insight: Manual feature engineering with validated outcomes performed best for acute pancreatitis phenotyping, but a simpler automated model using maximum lipase captured much of that performance.
clinical_relevance: For EHR-based case finding, thoughtfully chosen phenotype-aware outputs can nearly match more resource-intensive NLP and chart-review workflows.
method: Built a custom machine-learning model from manually curated structured claims/EHR features.
Added NLP-derived note features to test whether unstructured text improved case identification.
Compared this with a highly automated model trained on low-cost silver-standard outcomes (diagnosis-code count or maximum lipase).
evidence_signal: In evaluation, the custom model reached cv-AUC 0.89-0.91, the automated diagnosis-code model AUC 0.80, and the automated maximum-lipase model AUC 0.88; at 90% PPV, sensitivities were 92%, 45%, and 84%, respectively.
watch_item: The automated approach depended on a phenotype-specific lab signal, so results may not generalize to conditions without a similarly informative surrogate.
paper_title: A Comparison of Manual and Automated Approaches to Developing Computable Algorithms for Identifying Acute Pancreatitis
